title: A gated withdraw, then a blocked destination
summary: Alice pays Bob 12,000 mUSDC as two notes. Bob withdraws one to a payee. The operator then blocks an address, and Bob's withdrawal to it reverts although its proof is valid.
simplifications: One operator account deploys the contracts, attests the cohort, curates the blocklist, funds the deposits and relays every pool call. The spec gives these roles to separate parties.
The pool holds only this run's notes, so its anonymity set is far smaller than a busy pool's.
The audit committee is a single key (t = n = 1).
The wallet simulates each pool call and does not broadcast one that the pool refuses.
The chain is a local Anvil node.

plain.body: The operator checks account holders off-chain, then approves 10 keys in one batch, so no one can tell which approval belongs to whom. They can now use the pool; nobody has deposited yet.

title: The pool refuses Bob's withdraw to the blocked destination: BlockedDestination()

plain.title: A payout to a blocked address is refused
plain.body: Bob's payout carries a valid proof, but the pool refuses it because the destination is on the blocklist.

amount.why: The wallet simulates before it broadcasts, so the refused call never left it; only the RPC node that ran the simulation saw it. A call that reverts on-chain publishes its calldata.
